subject: Helix Health: MAP + roadtest plan for latency/concurrency benchmarking
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@helixhealth.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@helixhealth.io>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: MAP for performance validation — Helix Health / Redwood

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move into a formal mutual action plan (MAP) focused on performance: latency (TTFT), p95 latency, throughput at scale, and concurrency envelope. Goal: production readiness for our clinical triage assistant by end of December. Key asks:

- We'll provide a representative prompt set (attached: helix_perf_set_v1.csv) and a sample traffic profile (burst + steady-state).
- Can you produce a MAP that includes: detailed benchmark steps, target metrics, candidate model variants from Redwood catalog (including quantized options), and an evaluation schedule with checkpoints?
- Target SLOs: average TTFT < 250ms for 64-token replies and p95 < 400ms at 50 concurrent sessions. We may need results at 200 concurrent sessions as a stretch target.

We'd like a first-pass MAP and benchmark plan by Friday so we can sync with procurement on the 19th. Let me know if the timeline works.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
Helix Health
Attachments: helix_perf_set_v1.csv (csv)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@helixhealth.io>, Priya Singh <priya@helixhealth.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T12:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP for performance validation — Helix Health / Redwood

Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Appreciate the clear ask — this is doable. Draft MAP attached (RDW_MAP_Draft_Helix_20261112.docx). High-level plan:

1) Scope & workloads — we will run three tiers: dev (single-client, low concurrency), staging (50 concurrent), and stress (200 concurrent). We'll use your attached helix_perf_set_v1.csv.
2) Metrics — TTFT (time to first token), p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec), KV cache hit rate, and functional quality (task-specific accuracy on a held-out eval set).
3) Variants — we'll test: redwood-base-fp16, redwood-base-int8, redwood-proto-quant (4-bit), and a tuned 7B open model from the catalog. We'll include cost-per-1M-token estimates for each.
4) Test harness — Jonas will run the runner in our infra and produce per-variant runbooks; Marcus will instrument observability buckets for token breakdown.
5) Timeline — first-pass run and metrics by 2026-11-18; quality regressions check 2026-11-20; decision checkpoint + procurement handoff 2026-11-22.

Open questions for you:
- Confirm representative concurrency targets (50 + 200) and whether 64-token replies are representative of production.
- Any constraints on model variants (e.g., only quantized variants, or prefer open-source licenses)?

If that timeline looks good I'll kick off the runs and loop in our infra ops for reserved capacity during stress tests.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RDW_MAP_Draft_Helix_20261112.docx (docx)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP for performance validation — Helix Health / Redwood (internal)

Kim / Marcus,

Quick tech notes for the runs:
- Use sequence-length distribution from helix_perf_set_v1.csv: median 38 tokens request, 64 tokens response target.
- For concurrency 200, we'll need to enable continuous batching window of 15ms and warm KV cache with 10k warmup requests to approximate production cache hit patterns.
- Runner config: rdw-runner v3.4, tokenization sampling disabled, fixed seed for quality eval.
- For quantized variants we'll test int8 + 4-bit s8 quant configs; expect ~1.6-2.2x perf uplift on A100 and ~1.8-2.4x on H100 for TTFT.

I'll push a test job to the infra queue after Kimberly gives go.

-Jonas

Thanks Kim — draft looks good. Quick clarifications:

- Concurrency targets: 50 steady-state is firm; 200 is a mandatory stress target for our on-call SLAs. Please include explicit p95/p99 at 200 concurrency.
- Sequence lengths: we'll add a small set of longer-context prompts (200 token responses) to the staging run; attached (helix_sample_prompts_v1.jsonl).
- Model variants: favor quantized options first (cost constraints), but include one fp16 baseline for quality comparisons.

We'll expect the first-pass run results by 2026-11-18 as proposed. Procurement would like a short summary (one-pager) of the variance in latency vs. quality per-variant ahead of the 11/22 handoff.

Thanks,

Date: 2026-11-18T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP for performance validation — Helix Health / Redwood — run results and recommendation

Hi team,

Attached is the runbook and one-pager summary (Helix_Runbook_Results_20261118.pdf). High-level findings from the runs completed today:

- Workloads: used helix_perf_set_v1.csv + helix_sample_prompts_v1.jsonl; warmup included 12k requests to stabilize KV cache.
- Concurrency: 50 steady-state & 200 stress.
- TTFT (64-token target):
  - redwood-base-fp16: p50 95ms / p95 260ms / p99 410ms
  - redwood-base-int8: p50 70ms / p95 185ms / p99 320ms
  - redwood-proto-4bit: p50 60ms / p95 170ms / p99 300ms
  - tuned-7b-open-fp16: p50 120ms / p95 300ms / p99 480ms

- Quality (held-out eval accuracy): redwood-base-fp16 (baseline) 87.4% accuracy; redwood-base-int8 86.9% (-0.5pt); redwood-proto-4bit 86.6% (-0.8pt); tuned-7b-open 88.1% (+0.7pt).
- Cost estimate (approx): redwood-proto-4bit is ~0.42x cost of fp16 on token spend; int8 ~0.55x.

Recommendation: For Helix's cost/latency targets, redwood-proto-4bit hits the sweet spot — meets TTFT/p95 requirements at both 50 and 200 concurrencies with <1% quality regression versus baseline. If Helix requires the highest accuracy, tuned-7b-open is better quality but fails p99 at 200 concurrency.

Next steps:
- Kimberly to prepare procurement one-pager and pricing bands (due 2026-11-20).
- Jonas to provide infra cost estimate for sustained 200-concurrency reserved capacity (by 2026-11-20).
- Procurement handoff sync scheduled 2026-11-22 at 10:00am PT (calendar invite to follow).

If that aligns, I will mark this MAP Ready for Procurement and open a Dedicated capacity quote.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
